Key observations from the test image:
- Field-level view showing a distinct patch of completely dead/dried plants (center) surrounded by healthy green soybean plants
- Dead plants show brown, dried, bare stems with leaves dropped
- Patch pattern of plant death in an otherwise healthy field
- Some yellowing on adjacent plants

Top candidates: Phytophthora, Sudden_death_syndrome, Charcoal_Rot, Rhizoctonia. Let me check reference images.

The Charcoal Rot field view (bottom-left) shows the same pattern - rows of dead, dried, bare-stemmed plants surrounded by healthy green plants. Very similar to the test image. Let me check 2 more to confirm.

**Analysis:**

- **Test image**: Shows a distinct row/patch of completely dead, bare-stemmed, dried plants in a field, surrounded by healthy green soybean plants. Stems are tan/gray and completely leafless. Adjacent plants show some yellowing.

- **Charcoal Rot** reference (bottom-left): Shows the nearly identical field pattern — rows of dead, dried, leafless plants with pale/gray stems surrounded by healthy green plants. This matches the test image most closely.

- **Phytophthora**: Dead plants retain yellowing/wilting leaves — test image has bare stems, inconsistent.
- **SDS**: Shows interveinal chlorosis/necrosis on leaves; petioles remain; the test shows complete leaf drop.
- **Brown Stem Rot**: Smaller patches, interveinal chlorosis visible; less extreme stem drying.
- **Fusarium/Rhizoctonia**: Primarily close-up stem/root diseases, seedling-focused, not this field-scale patch pattern.

The pattern of complete plant death in strips/patches with pale, dried, bare stems in an otherwise healthy field is the hallmark field presentation of Charcoal Rot.
